I reviewed the snippet around L499 in `Debug/handeye_visualizer.py`.

### Short answer
- Yes. `cam_point` is the 3D point of the selected pixel at depth `Z`, expressed in the camera’s coordinate frame (in mm).

### What each part means
- `x_norm, y_norm`: normalized image coordinates for pixel `(u, v)` (after optional undistortion).
- `cam_point = [x_norm*Z, y_norm*Z, Z]`: back-projection of the pixel to 3D in the camera frame at depth `Z` (pinhole model).
- Then `C_reflect_x @ cam_point` flips camera X to match this app’s display convention.
- `pZ = t_bc + R_bc @ cam_point`: transforms that camera-frame point into the robot base/world frame.
- `ray_dir`: just a unit direction vector to draw the viewing ray; not the point location.

Summary:
- `cam_point` = object point in camera coords at depth `Z`; `pZ` = the same point in base coords.
